guide.title: Financial District, San Francisco: the Ferry Building, Montgomery Street and the downtown plazas
guide.intro: San Francisco's Financial District is a quarter of banks, exchanges and towers that ends at the water. The Ferry Building stands on the Embarcadero at the foot of Market Street, its marketplace open daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm, with the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market outside it on Saturday, Tuesday and Thursday. Embarcadero Center runs four buildings across four blocks. Montgomery Street carries the older banking houses, among them the Kohl Building, the Mills Building and Tower and the Italian American Bank, and the Transamerica Pyramid rises from 600 Montgomery Street above the redwoods of Redwood Park. California, Sansome and Pine Streets hold the exchanges. Threaded between all of them is a chain of privately owned public open spaces: sun terraces, sunken plazas, atriums and one alley with a living plant wall.

sections.heading: The Embarcadero and the Ferry Building
sections.body:
The Ferry Building stands along the Embarcadero at the foot of Market Street. It is San Francisco Landmark No. 90, designated in 1977, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 as the Union Ferry Depot, reference number 78000760. It opened on 13 July 1898. The marketplace inside the nave opens daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm and closes on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day; hours for individual businesses vary. Outside it, at Embarcadero and Market Streets, Foodwise runs the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market on Saturday from 8am to 2pm and on Tuesday and Thursday from 10am to 2pm, year round.

Embarcadero Plaza is a civic plaza of 4.14 acres at 10 Market Street; the Vaillancourt Fountain stands in it. Maritime Plaza is a civic plaza of 2.01 acres at 285 Washington Street, and the Alcoa Building at 300 Clay Street adjoins it. Embarcadero Center is four buildings spanning four blocks, with office space, hundreds of shops, restaurants, services and a multiplex cinema; development began in 1968 and concluded in 1983, and construction of each of the four buildings was completed over a ten-year span between 1971 and 1981.

North of the Ferry Building the piers carry federal citations of their own. Pier One, at the Embarcadero and Washington Street, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1999, reference number 98001551. Piers 1, 1 1/2, 3 and 5 were listed together as the Central Embarcadero Piers Historic District, reference number 02001390, certified 20 November 2002, with a period of significance running from 1918 to 1952.

sections.heading: The banking blocks and their open spaces
sections.body:
Montgomery Street is the older spine. The Kohl Building at 400 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 161, designated in 1983; the A. Borel & Company Building at 440 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 109, designated in 1980; the Italian American Bank at 460 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 110, designated in 1980. The Mills Building & Tower at 220-232 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 76, designated in 1975, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977, reference number 77000334. One Montgomery Street, which the Article 10 register names for the Crocker National Bank, is San Francisco Landmark No. 297, designated in 2022. The Transamerica Pyramid stands at 600 Montgomery Street, over 850 feet tall, clad in white quartz and carrying over 3,000 windows; William Pereira designed it and it was completed in 1972, and a remastering of the interiors with Foster + Partners was completed in 2024.

On California, Sansome and Pine Streets: the Bank of California at 400 California Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 3, designated in 1968; the Royal Globe Insurance Building at 210 Sansome Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 160, designated in 1983; the Federal Reserve Bank Building at 400 Sansome Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 158, designated in 1983, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989, reference number 89000009. The mural in the Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Tower at 155 Sansome Street, The Allegory of California, is San Francisco Landmark No. 298, designated in 2022. The Merchants Exchange at 465 California Street, the Russ Building at 235 Montgomery Street, the Shell Building at 100 Bush Street and the Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Trading Room at 301 Pine Street each carry Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code. On Commercial Street, the U.S. Mint & Subtreasury Building at 608-610 Commercial Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 34, designated in 1970, and PG&E Old Station J at 565-569 Commercial Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 142, designated in 1981, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1986, reference number 86003514. Storeship sites lie under the street corners: APOLLO at the northwest corner of Sacramento and Battery Streets, reference number 91000561, and NIANTIC at the northwest corner of Clay and Sansome Streets, reference number 91000563, both certified 16 May 1991.

The district's seating is largely privately owned public open space. Redwood Park at 535 Washington Street, established in 1972, is described in the City's survey as redwood trees at the foot of the Transamerica Pyramid, a tall water fountain, sculptures and ample seating. 101 California Street has about 1,000 linear feet of terraced-step seating; 555 California Street has a central pool and 24 small wooden bench seats at the eastern edge of its elevated plaza, with Masayuki Nagare's black granite Transcendence on the west side; 456 Montgomery Street is a sunken plaza with escalator access, 72 feet of linear seating, flowers and small water fountains. Trinity Alley at 333 Bush Street is a pedestrian walkway with about 50 linear seats and a living plant wall. Upstairs there are three more: the sun terrace on the sixth floor at 150 California Street, the view terrace on the fifteenth floor at 343 Sansome Street, and the sun terrace on the third floor of Crocker Galleria at 50 Post Street.

West along Sutter, Post and Bush Streets the buildings and the dining rooms run together. The Hallidie Building at 130-150 Sutter Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 37, designated in 1971, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971, reference number 71000185. The Hunter-Dulin Building at 111 Sutter Street, at Montgomery Street, was listed in 1997, reference number 97000348. The Mechanics' Institute at 57-65 Post Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 134, designated in 1981, and holds a Beaux Arts library of over 100,000 books and a chess club. The S.F. Curb Mining Exchange at 350 Bush Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 113, designated in 1980, and the Crown Zellerbach Building at 1 Bush Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 183, designated in 1987, with a sunken plaza of 1959 at its foot. Lotta's Fountain stands where Market, Geary and Kearny Streets meet: San Francisco Landmark No. 73, designated in 1975, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975 as the Lotta Crabtree Fountain, reference number 75000475.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
The Ferry Building is reachable by several ferry lines, all BART lines, many MUNI lines, the F Market streetcar and the California Street cable car line, and the F Market historic streetcars stop at the building. Validated parking is available at the ProPark lot at Embarcadero and Washington.

The addresses that matter: the Ferry Building, on the Embarcadero at the foot of Market Street. The Ferry Plaza Farmers Market, at Embarcadero and Market Streets. Embarcadero Plaza, 10 Market Street. Maritime Plaza, 285 Washington Street. The Transamerica Pyramid, 600 Montgomery Street, with Redwood Park at 535 Washington Street. The Mechanics' Institute, 57-65 Post Street. Crocker Galleria, 50 Post Street. Tadich Grill, 240 California Street. Sam's Grill & Seafood, 374 Bush Street, and Sam's Tavern at 368 Bush Street. Punch Line Comedy Club, 444 Battery Street.

Much of the ground floor of this district is indoors and keeps office hours. The open spaces at 101 California Street, 345 California Street, 456 Montgomery Street, 555 California Street and 333 Bush Street are open at all times. The terraces are not: 150 California Street opens 9am to 6pm Monday to Friday, 343 Sansome Street 10AM to 5PM Monday to Friday, 350 Bush Street 7AM to 6PM Monday to Friday, and Crocker Galleria's third-floor terrace 6am to 7pm Monday to Saturday.

faq.question: When is the Ferry Building open, and when is the farmers market?
faq.answer: The Ferry Building marketplace opens daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm and closes on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day; hours for individual businesses inside vary. The Ferry Plaza Farmers Market, run by Foodwise outside the building at Embarcadero and Market Streets, opens Saturday from 8am to 2pm and Tuesday and Thursday from 10am to 2pm, year round. The building is San Francisco Landmark No. 90, designated in 1977, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 as the Union Ferry Depot, reference number 78000760. It opened on 13 July 1898.

faq.question: Can I go into the Mechanics' Institute, and when is the chess room open?
faq.answer: The Mechanics' Institute is at 57-65 Post Street and the telephone number is (415) 393-0101. The library opens Monday to Friday from 10am to 6pm, until 8pm on Tuesday and Thursday, and Saturday from 10am to 5pm. The chess room opens Monday to Friday from 10am to 6pm and Saturday from 10am to 5pm. The building opens Monday to Friday from 8.15am, until 6pm and until 8pm on Tuesday and Thursday, and Saturday from 9.30am to 5.30pm. Both are closed on Sunday. It holds a Beaux Arts library of over 100,000 books, a chess club with a Grandmaster-in-Residence programme, and meeting rooms on the 3rd and 4th floors. The building is San Francisco Landmark No. 134, designated in 1981.

faq.question: Where can I sit down here without buying anything?
faq.answer: The district is full of privately owned public open spaces. Open at all times: the plaza at 101 California Street, with about 1,000 linear feet of terraced-step seating and cushions available; the elevated plaza at 555 California Street, with a central pool and 24 small wooden bench seats at its eastern edge; the sunken plaza at 456 Montgomery Street, with 72 feet of linear seating, 8 movable chairs and 2 tables; the plaza and two snippets at 345 California Street; and Trinity Alley at 333 Bush Street, with about 50 linear seats, movable tables and a living plant wall. Redwood Park at 535 Washington Street has over 100 linear seats on boxes and room for more than 30 on the steps, no food service and no restrooms; hours are not posted and the City's survey records it closing before 6pm. Upstairs, 150 California Street opens 9am to 6pm Monday to Friday, 343 Sansome Street 10AM to 5PM Monday to Friday, and Crocker Galleria's third-floor terrace 6am to 7pm Monday to Saturday.

faq.question: Which buildings here carry a register citation?
faq.answer: On the Article 10 register: the Bank of California at 400 California Street, San Francisco Landmark No. 3, designated in 1968; the U.S. Mint & Subtreasury Building at 608-610 Commercial Street, No. 34, designated in 1970; the Hallidie Building at 130-150 Sutter Street, No. 37, designated in 1971; Lotta's Fountain, No. 73, designated in 1975; the Mills Building & Tower at 220-232 Montgomery Street, No. 76, designated in 1975; the Ferry Building, No. 90, designated in 1977; the A. Borel & Company Building at 440 Montgomery Street, No. 109, and the Italian American Bank at 460 Montgomery Street, No. 110, both designated in 1980; the S.F. Curb Mining Exchange at 350 Bush Street, No. 113, designated in 1980; the Mechanics' Institute at 57-65 Post Street, No. 134, designated in 1981; PG&E Old Station J at 565-569 Commercial Street, No. 142, designated in 1981; the Buich Building, which holds Tadich Grill at 240-242 California Street, No. 145, designated in 1981; the Flatiron Building at 540-548 Market Street, No. 155, designated in 1982; the Federal Reserve Bank Building at 400 Sansome Street, No. 158, and the Royal Globe Insurance Building at 210 Sansome Street, No. 160, both designated in 1983; the Kohl Building at 400 Montgomery Street, No. 161, designated in 1983; the Crown Zellerbach Building at 1 Bush Street, No. 183, designated in 1987; One Montgomery Street, No. 297, and The Allegory of California mural at 155 Sansome Street, No. 298, both designated in 2022. On the federal register: the Hallidie Building, reference number 71000185; the Mills Building and Tower, 77000334; Lotta Crabtree Fountain, 75000475; Union Ferry Depot, 78000760; Pacific Gas and Electric Company Substation J, 86003514; the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, 89000009; the APOLLO and NIANTIC storeship sites, 91000561 and 91000563; the Hunter-Dulin Building, 97000348; Pier One, 98001551; and the Central Embarcadero Piers Historic District, 02001390.

faq.question: Which of the old dining rooms publish their hours?
faq.answer: Tadich Grill at 240 California Street opens Monday to Friday from 11:00am to 9:00pm and Saturday from 4:00pm to 9:00pm, and closes on Sunday; the telephone number is (415) 391-1849. Sam's Grill & Seafood at 374 Bush Street opens Monday to Friday from 11:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Saturday from 5:30 PM to 9:00 PM, closing on Sundays and major holidays; Sam's Tavern next door at 368 Bush Street runs its kitchen Monday to Friday from 9:30 AM to 9:00 PM with the bar until 10pm, and Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Perbacco at 230 California Street opens Tuesday to Friday from 11:30 am to 9:00 pm and Saturday from 5:30 pm to 9:00 pm, and closes on Sunday. Wayfare Tavern at 201 Pine Street opens Sunday to Wednesday from 11:30 am to 9:00 pm and Thursday to Saturday from 11:30 am to 10:00 pm. For Schroeder's at 240 Front Street, no source states opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Ferry Building
places.address: The Embarcadero at Market Street, San Francisco, CA 94111
places.summary: The terminal building on the Embarcadero at the foot of Market Street, with a marketplace along its nave. The marketplace opens daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm and closes on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day; hours for individual businesses vary. It is San Francisco Landmark No. 90, designated in 1977, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 as the Union Ferry Depot, reference number 78000760.
places.history: The building opened on 13 July 1898. It is reachable by several ferry lines, all BART lines, many MUNI lines, the F Market streetcar and the California Street cable car line, the F Market historic streetcars stop at the building, and validated parking is available at the ProPark lot at Embarcadero and Washington.

places.name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
places.address: Embarcadero and Market Streets, San Francisco, CA 94111
places.summary: The market Foodwise runs outside the Ferry Building at Embarcadero and Market Streets. It opens on Saturday from 8am to 2pm and on Tuesday and Thursday from 10am to 2pm, year round.
places.history: The market stands on the Embarcadero side of the Ferry Building, whose own marketplace opens daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm.

places.name: Embarcadero Plaza
places.summary: The 4.14-acre civic plaza at 10 Market Street, at the foot of Market Street. The Vaillancourt Fountain stands in it.
places.history: No source states opening hours for the plaza, so none are given here.

places.name: Maritime Plaza
places.summary: An elevated civic plaza of 2.01 acres at 285 Washington Street.
places.history: The Alcoa Building at 300 Clay Street adjoins the plaza.

places.name: Pier One
places.address: Pier One, The Embarcadero at Washington Street, San Francisco, CA
places.summary: The pier building on the Embarcadero at Washington Street. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1999, reference number 98001551, certified 5 January 1999.
places.history: Piers 1, 1 1/2, 3 and 5 were listed together as the Central Embarcadero Piers Historic District, reference number 02001390, certified 20 November 2002.

places.name: Central Embarcadero Piers Historic District
places.summary: The district of Piers 1, 1 1/2, 3 and 5 on the Embarcadero. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2002, reference number 02001390, certified 20 November 2002.
places.history: The period of significance runs from 1918 to 1952. Pier One carries a National Register listing of its own, reference number 98001551, certified 5 January 1999.

places.name: Embarcadero Center
places.summary: Four buildings spanning four blocks, with office space, hundreds of shops, restaurants, services and a multiplex cinema. The complex has earned LEED certification, and the owner is given as Boston Properties.
places.history: It was built in phases over 15 years: development began in 1968 and concluded in 1983, and construction of each of the four buildings was completed over a ten-year span between 1971 and 1981. The pedestrian mall through Centers 1, 2 and 3 is a privately owned public open space of 1985, on the ground and second levels, with 30 tables and 107 chairs, open at all times.

places.name: Transamerica Pyramid
places.summary: The tapered tower at 600 Montgomery Street, standing over 850 feet, clad in white quartz and carrying over 3,000 windows.
places.history: William Pereira designed the building and it was completed in 1972. A remastering of the interiors with Foster + Partners was completed in 2024. Redwood Park lies at its foot, at 535 Washington Street.

places.name: Redwood Park
places.summary: A privately owned public open space of 1972 at 535 Washington Street, which the City's survey describes as redwood trees at the foot of the Transamerica Pyramid, a tall water fountain, sculptures and ample seating. There are over 100 linear seats on boxes and room for more than 30 on the steps. There is no food service and there are no restrooms.
places.history: Hours are not posted, and the City's survey records the park closing before 6pm.

places.name: Bank of California
places.summary: The banking house at 400 California Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 3, designated in 1968.
places.history: The Merchants Exchange stands along the same street at 465 California Street, and the Hind Building, which holds Perbacco, at 230 California Street.

places.name: The Kohl Building
places.summary: The office building at 400 Montgomery Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 161, designated in 1983.
places.history: The Article 10 record names it the Alvinza Hayward Building as well as the Kohl Building.

places.name: A. Borel & Company Building
places.summary: The building at 440 Montgomery Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 109, designated in 1980.
places.history: The Italian American Bank at 460 Montgomery Street stands in the same block and is San Francisco Landmark No. 110, designated in 1980.

places.name: Italian American Bank
places.summary: The bank building at 460 Montgomery Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 110, designated in 1980.
places.history: The Kohl Building at 400 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 161, designated in 1983, and the A. Borel & Company Building at 440 Montgomery Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 109, designated in 1980.

places.name: Mills Building & Tower
places.summary: The building and tower at 220-232 Montgomery Street, which also fronts 220 Bush Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 76, designated in 1975, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977, reference number 77000334.
places.history: The National Register record gives the address as 220 Montgomery Street and 220 Bush Street, with a certification date of 13 April 1977.

places.name: Royal Globe Insurance Building
places.summary: The insurance building at 210 Sansome Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 160, designated in 1983.
places.history: The Federal Reserve Bank Building stands along the same street at 400 Sansome Street and is San Francisco Landmark No. 158, designated in 1983.

places.name: Federal Reserve Bank Building
places.summary: The bank building at 400 Sansome Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 158, designated in 1983, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989 as the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, reference number 89000009, certified 31 July 1989.
places.history: Arman's bronze Hermes and Dionysus - Monument to Analysis stands on the front steps at the sidewalk along Sansome Street and is always accessible.

places.name: Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Tower
places.summary: The tower at 155 Sansome Street. The mural it holds, The Allegory of California, is San Francisco Landmark No. 298, designated in 2022.
places.history: The Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Trading Room stands at 301 Pine Street.

places.name: Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Trading Room
places.summary: The trading room building at 301 Pine Street. It carries Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code.
places.history: The Pacific Coast Stock Exchange Tower stands at 155 Sansome Street and holds the mural The Allegory of California.

places.name: Merchants Exchange
places.summary: The Merchants Exchange at 465 California Street carries Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code.
places.history: No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Russ Building
places.summary: The Russ Building at 235 Montgomery Street carries Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code.
places.history: No source states its construction date, so none is given here.

places.name: Shell Building
places.summary: The Shell Building, also recorded as the Shell Oil Company Building, at 100 Bush Street. It carries Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code.
places.history: No source states its construction date, so none is given here.

places.name: Crown Zellerbach Building
places.summary: The tower at 1 Bush Street with a sunken plaza at its foot. San Francisco Landmark No. 183, designated in 1987. The plaza is a privately owned public open space of 1959, open at all times, planted with willow trees, with seating limited to the steps.
places.history: David Tolerton's bronze fountain stands on the west side of the sunken open space, along the Sansome Street frontage.

places.name: S.F. Curb Mining Exchange
places.summary: The exchange building at 350 Bush Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 113, designated in 1980.
places.history: The 2019 development on the site carries a privately owned public open space: an indoor park at 350 Bush Street, snippets at 465 Pine Street and a view terrace at 500 Pine Street, open 7AM to 6PM Monday to Friday, with restrooms.

places.name: U.S. Mint & Subtreasury Building
places.summary: The building at 608-610 Commercial Street that the Article 10 register names the U.S. Mint & Subtreasury Building. San Francisco Landmark No. 34, designated in 1970.
places.history: PG&E Old Station J stands along the same street at 565-569 Commercial Street and is San Francisco Landmark No. 142, designated in 1981.

places.name: PG&E Old Station J
places.summary: The substation building at 565-569 Commercial Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 142, designated in 1981, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1986 as Pacific Gas and Electric Company Substation J, reference number 86003514, certified 29 December 1986.
places.history: The National Register record gives the address as 565 Commercial and 568 Sacramento Streets. The Leidesdorff Street frontage at 222 Leidesdorff carries Category I under Article 11 of the San Francisco Planning Code.

places.name: APOLLO (Storeship)
places.summary: The buried storeship site at the northwest corner of Sacramento and Battery Streets. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1991, reference number 91000561, certified 16 May 1991.
places.history: Nothing of the ship stands above ground.

places.name: NIANTIC (Storeship)
places.summary: The buried storeship site at the northwest corner of Clay and Sansome Streets. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1991, reference number 91000563, certified 16 May 1991.
places.history: Nothing of the ship stands above ground. The APOLLO storeship site sits at the northwest corner of Sacramento and Battery Streets, reference number 91000561.

places.name: 456 Montgomery Street
places.summary: A sunken plaza at 456 Montgomery Street, a privately owned public open space of 1983, open at all times, with 72 feet of linear seating, 8 movable chairs and 2 tables, flowers and small water fountains.
places.history: The plaza sits below the sidewalk and is reached by escalator.

places.name: 101 California Street
places.summary: The plaza at 101 California Street, a privately owned public open space of 1982, open at all times, with roughly 1,000 linear feet of terraced-step seating, cushions available, and food service on site.
places.history: Two other privately owned public open spaces stand along the same street, at 345 California Street and 150 California Street.

places.name: 345 California Street
places.summary: A plaza and two snippets at 345 California Street, a privately owned public open space of 1986, open at all times, with a sandwich shop and a cafe.
places.history: The two snippets sit on either side of the building's main entrance, connected by a walkway.

places.name: 150 California Street
places.summary: A sun terrace at 150 California Street, on the sixth floor, a privately owned public open space of 2000, open 9am to 6pm Monday to Friday, with nine tables and 36 movable chairs.
places.history: The district's other upper-level open spaces are the view terrace at 343 Sansome Street and the sun terrace at Crocker Galleria, 50 Post Street.

places.name: 343 Sansome Street
places.summary: A view terrace on the fifteenth floor at 343 Sansome Street, a privately owned public open space of 1990, open 10AM to 5PM Monday to Friday; the restroom key is held by the lobby attendant.
places.history: Joan Brown's tiled obelisk Four Seasons stands in the roof garden, and Pol Bury's stainless steel and marble water sculpture L'Octagon in the Sacramento Street lobby; both are accessible from 9 to 5.

places.name: Citigroup Center
places.summary: The ground-floor atrium at 1 Sansome Street, a privately owned public open space of 1983, finished in marble and glass, with a cafe and deli and restrooms.
places.history: Stirling Calder's bronze Star Maiden stands on the north side of the ground-floor atrium and is accessible during business hours.

places.name: 555 California Street
places.summary: The elevated plaza at 555 California Street, a privately owned public open space of 1969, open at all times, with a central pool and 24 small wooden bench seats at its eastern edge.
places.history: Masayuki Nagare's black granite Transcendence stands on the west side of the elevated plaza and is always accessible.

places.name: 325 Battery Street
places.summary: Three bronzes stand at 325 Battery Street: an untitled work by Fritz Koenig at the spiral staircase on Commercial Street, Creazione by Dimitri Hadzi, and The Universality of Wisdom by Arman at the Federal Reserve steps on Battery Street.
places.history: All three are always accessible.

places.name: 425 Battery Street
places.summary: The General Harrison, by Curtis Hollenback and Topher Delaney, at 425 Battery Street: unearthed ship parts set into the public right-of-way in front of the building. It is always accessible.
places.history: The work was approved under case 2000.613X.

places.name: Trinity Alley
places.summary: A pedestrian walkway at 333 Bush Street, a privately owned public open space of 1983, open at all times, with roughly 50 linear seats, movable tables, food all along the alley and a living plant wall.
places.history: The alley runs through the block at 333 Bush Street.

places.name: Hallidie Building
places.summary: The building at 130-150 Sutter Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 37, designated in 1971, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971, reference number 71000185, certified 19 November 1971.
places.history: The Hunter-Dulin Building is at 111 Sutter Street, at Montgomery Street.

places.name: Hunter-Dulin Building
places.summary: The office building at 111 Sutter Street, at Montgomery Street. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1997, reference number 97000348, certified 17 April 1997.
places.history: The Hallidie Building stands along the same street at 130-150 Sutter Street and is San Francisco Landmark No. 37, designated in 1971.

places.name: The Mechanics' Institute
places.summary: A Beaux Arts library of over 100,000 books with a chess club, at 57-65 Post Street; the telephone number is (415) 393-0101. The library opens Monday to Friday from 10am to 6pm, until 8pm on Tuesday and Thursday, and Saturday from 10am to 5pm. The chess room opens Monday to Friday from 10am to 6pm and Saturday from 10am to 5pm. The building opens Monday to Friday from 8.15am, until 6pm and until 8pm on Tuesday and Thursday, and Saturday from 9.30am to 5.30pm. Both are closed on Sunday. San Francisco Landmark No. 134, designated in 1981.
places.history: The chess club runs a Grandmaster-in-Residence programme, and there are meeting rooms on the 3rd and 4th floors. The institute is a nonprofit with EIN 94-1254644.

places.name: Crocker Galleria
places.summary: A shopping centre at 50 Post Street. A sun terrace on the third floor, open 6am to 7pm Monday to Saturday, with twenty-four benches each 7 feet 8 inches long, restrooms, and eight large planters with trees.
places.history: The terrace is on the third floor of the shopping centre, reached along a hallway.

places.name: One Montgomery Street
places.summary: The building at 1-25 Montgomery Street, which the Article 10 register names One Montgomery Street (Crocker National Bank). San Francisco Landmark No. 297, designated in 2022.
places.history: Lotta's Fountain stands where Market, Geary and Kearny Streets meet and is San Francisco Landmark No. 73, designated in 1975.

places.name: Lotta's Fountain
places.summary: The fountain standing where Market, Geary and Kearny Streets meet. San Francisco Landmark No. 73, designated in 1975, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975 as the Lotta Crabtree Fountain, reference number 75000475, certified 20 June 1975.
places.history: The Flatiron Building stands along Market Street at 540-548 Market Street and is San Francisco Landmark No. 155, designated in 1982.

places.name: Flatiron Building
places.summary: The wedge-shaped building at 540-548 Market Street, where Market, Sutter and Sansome Streets meet. San Francisco Landmark No. 155, designated in 1982.

places.summary: An Italian restaurant at 230 California Street; the telephone number is (415) 955-0663. It opens Tuesday to Friday from 11:30 am to 9:00 pm and Saturday from 5:30 pm to 9:00 pm, and closes on Sunday.

places.summary: A tavern and dining room at 201 Pine Street, open Sunday to Wednesday from 11:30 am to 9:00 pm and Thursday to Saturday from 11:30 am to 10:00 pm.

places.history: Sam's Grill & Seafood is at 374 Bush Street and keeps different hours.

places.name: Punch Line Comedy Club
places.summary: A comedy club at 444 Battery Street; the telephone number is 415.397.7573. It is operated by Live Nation.
places.history: The club runs on a per-show schedule rather than fixed opening hours, so none are given here.

entries.name: Ferry Building
entries.note: Opened on 13 July 1898 at the foot of Market Street; San Francisco Landmark No. 90, designated in 1977, with a marketplace open daily from 6:00am to 10:00pm.

entries.name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
entries.note: Foodwise runs it outside the Ferry Building on Saturday from 8am to 2pm and on Tuesday and Thursday from 10am to 2pm, year round.

entries.name: Transamerica Pyramid
entries.note: William Pereira's tower at 600 Montgomery Street, over 850 feet, in white quartz with over 3,000 windows; completed in 1972 and remastered inside by 2024.

entries.name: Redwood Park
entries.note: Redwoods, a tall water fountain and seating at the foot of the Pyramid, 535 Washington Street; hours are not posted and the park closes before 6pm.

entries.name: Tadich Grill
entries.note: A dining room and counter at 240 California Street, in the Buich Building, San Francisco Landmark No. 145, designated in 1981.

entries.name: Sam's Grill & Seafood
entries.note: Private booths and mesquite-grilled fish at 374 Bush Street, open Monday to Friday from 11:00 AM and Saturday from 5:30 PM.

entries.name: Wayfare Tavern
entries.note: Marble floors, tufted leather booths, a gold leaf mural honouring the Barbary Coast and a green serpentine stone bar, at 201 Pine Street.

entries.name: The Mechanics' Institute
entries.note: A Beaux Arts library of over 100,000 books and a chess room at 57-65 Post Street; San Francisco Landmark No. 134, designated in 1981.

entries.name: Crocker Galleria
entries.note: The sun terrace on the third floor at 50 Post Street opens 6am to 7pm Monday to Saturday, with twenty-four benches and eight planters of trees.

entries.name: Lotta's Fountain
entries.note: The fountain where Market, Geary and Kearny Streets meet; San Francisco Landmark No. 73, designated in 1975, and on the National Register, 75000475.

entries.name: Trinity Alley
entries.note: A pedestrian walkway at 333 Bush Street with about 50 linear seats, movable tables, food along its length and a living plant wall, open at all times.

entries.name: 343 Sansome Street
entries.note: A fifteenth-floor terrace open 10AM to 5PM on weekdays; Joan Brown's Four Seasons is in the roof garden and Pol Bury's L'Octagon in the lobby.

entries.name: Embarcadero Center
entries.note: Four buildings across four blocks, built between 1971 and 1981, with shops, restaurants, a cinema and an open pedestrian mall of 1985.

entries.name: Punch Line Comedy Club
entries.note: A comedy club at 444 Battery Street operated by Live Nation, running on a per-show schedule.
